title_en: Company Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of regulating the organization and conduct of companies, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of companies, shareholders, employees and creditors, improving the modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics, promoting entrepreneurship, maintaining the social and economic order, and facilitating the development of the socialist market economy.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, a "company" refers to a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company established within the territory of the People's Republic of China in accordance with this Law.

Article 3 A company is an enterprise legal person, which has independent legal person property and enjoys the right to legal person property. A company shall be liable for its debts with all of its property.
The legitimate rights and interests of a company shall be protected by law and shall not be infringed upon.

Article 4 A shareholder of a limited liability company shall be liable to the company to the extent of its subscribed capital contribution; a shareholder of a joint stock limited company shall be liable to the company to the extent of its subscribed shares.
Shareholders of a company shall, according to law, enjoy rights such as receiving returns on assets, participating in major decision-making, and selecting managers.

Article 5 When establishing a company, the company's articles of association shall be formulated according to law. The company's articles of association shall be binding on the company, its shareholders, directors, supervisors, and senior officers.

Article 6 A company shall have its own name. The name of a company shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State.
The right to the name of a company shall be protected by law.

Article 7 A limited liability company established in accordance with this Law shall indicate the words "limited liability company" or "company limited" in its name.
A joint stock limited company established in accordance with this Law shall indicate the words "joint stock limited company" or "company limited by shares" in its name.
Article 8 The domicile of a company shall be the place where its principal office is located.

Article 9 The business scope of a company shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association. A company may amend its articles of association to change its business scope.
Where items within the business scope of a company are subject to approval as provided for by laws or administrative regulations, such approval shall be obtained according to law.

Article 10 The legal representative of a company shall be a director or manager who represents the company in executing its affairs, in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association.
Where a director or manager serving as the legal representative resigns from office, he or she shall be deemed to have simultaneously resigned as the legal representative.
Where the legal representative resigns, the company shall appoint a new legal representative within thirty days from the date of such resignation.

Article 11 The legal consequences of civil activities conducted by the legal representative in the name of the company shall be borne by the company.
Restrictions on the authority of the legal representative imposed by the company's articles of association or the shareholders' meeting shall not be invoked against a bona fide counterparty.
Where the legal representative causes harm to another person in the performance of his or her duties, the company shall bear civil liability. After bearing civil liability, the company may, in accordance with the law or the company's articles of association, seek recourse against the legal representative who is at fault.

Article 12 Where a limited liability company is converted into a joint stock limited company, it shall meet the conditions for a joint stock limited company as prescribed by this Law. Where a joint stock limited company is converted into a limited liability company, it shall meet the conditions for a limited liability company as prescribed by this Law.
Where a limited liability company is converted into a joint stock limited company, or where a joint stock limited company is converted into a limited liability company, the debts and claims of the company prior to the conversion shall be succeeded to by the company after conversion.

Article 13 A company may establish subsidiaries. A subsidiary shall have the status of a legal person and shall independently bear civil liability according to law.
A company may establish branches. A branch shall not have the status of a legal person, and its civil liability shall be borne by the company.

Article 14 A company may invest in other enterprises.
Where the law provides that a company shall not become an investor bearing joint and several liability for the debts of the enterprise in which it invests, such provision shall prevail.

Article 15 Where a company invests in other enterprises or provides guarantees to others, it shall be subject to a resolution of the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association; where the company's articles of association impose limits on the total amount of investments or guarantees, or on the amount of individual investments or guarantees, such limits shall not be exceeded.
Where a company provides a guarantee to a shareholder or actual controller of the company, it shall be subject to a resolution of the shareholders' meeting.
The shareholder specified in the preceding paragraph, or a shareholder controlled by the actual controller specified in the preceding paragraph, shall not participate in the voting on the matter specified in the preceding paragraph. Such matter shall be passed by more than half of the voting rights held by other shareholders present at the meeting.

Article 16 A company shall protect the legitimate rights and interests of its employees, sign labor contracts with its employees according to law, participate in social insurance, strengthen labor protection, and achieve safe production.
A company shall adopt various forms to strengthen vocational education and on-the-job training for its employees to improve their quality.

Article 17 Employees of a company shall, in accordance with the Trade Union Law of the People's Republic of China, organize trade unions, carry out trade union activities, and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of employees. A company shall provide necessary conditions for the activities of its trade union. The trade union shall, on behalf of the employees, sign a collective contract with the company according to law regarding matters such as labor remuneration, working hours, rest and leave, labor safety and hygiene, and insurance and welfare.
A company shall, in accordance with the Constitution and relevant laws, establish and improve a democratic management system with the employees' congress as its basic form, and implement democratic management through the employees' congress or other forms.
When a company studies and decides on matters such as restructuring, dissolution, applying for bankruptcy, major operational issues, or formulating important rules and regulations, it shall solicit opinions from its trade union and, through the employees' congress or other forms, solicit opinions and suggestions from the employees.

Article 18 In a company, the organization of the Communist Party of China shall be established in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Communist Party of China, and Party activities shall be carried out. The company shall provide necessary conditions for the activities of the Party organization.

Article 19 When engaging in business activities, a company shall comply with laws and regulations, observe social morality and business ethics, act in good faith, and accept supervision from the government and the public.

Article 20 When engaging in business activities, a company shall fully consider the interests of stakeholders such as the company's employees and consumers, as well as social public interests such as ecological and environmental protection, and shall bear social responsibility.
The State encourages companies to participate in public welfare activities and to disclose social responsibility reports.

Article 21 A shareholder of a company shall abide by laws, administrative regulations and the company's articles of association, exercise shareholder rights according to law, and shall not abuse shareholder rights to harm the interests of the company or other shareholders.
Where a shareholder of a company causes losses to the company or other shareholders by abusing shareholder rights, the shareholder shall bear compensation liability.

Article 22 The controlling shareholders, actual controllers, directors, supervisors, and senior officers of a company shall not use affiliated relationships to harm the interests of the company.
Where the preceding paragraph is violated and losses are caused to the company, compensation liability shall be borne.

Article 23 Where a shareholder of a company abuses the independent legal person status of the company and the limited liability of shareholders to evade debts and seriously harms the interests of the company's creditors, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts.
Where a shareholder uses two or more companies under its control to commit the act specified in the preceding paragraph, each company shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of any one of those companies.
In a company with only one shareholder, if the shareholder cannot prove that the company's property is independent of its own property, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts.

Article 24 Meetings and voting of the shareholders' meeting, board of directors, and board of supervisors of a company may be conducted by electronic means of communication, unless otherwise provided for in the company's articles of association.
Article 25 Resolutions of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors of a company that contravene laws or administrative regulations shall be void.

Article 26 Where the convening procedures or voting methods of a meeting of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors of a company violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, or where the content of a resolution violates the company's articles of association, a shareholder may, within sixty days from the date the resolution is made, request the People's Court to revoke it. However, this shall not apply if the defect in the convening procedures or voting methods of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors is only minor and does not have a substantive impact on the resolution.
A shareholder who was not notified to attend the shareholders' meeting may, within sixty days from the date it knew or should have known of the adoption of the shareholders' meeting resolution, request the People's Court to revoke it; if the right to revoke is not exercised within one year from the date the resolution was made, the right to revoke shall be extinguished.

Article 28 Where a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors of a company is declared void, revoked, or confirmed as not established by the People's Court, the company shall apply to the company registration authority to cancel any registration that has been made based on such resolution.
Where a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors is declared void, revoked, or confirmed as not established by the People's Court, the civil legal relationship formed between the company and a bona fide counterparty based on such resolution shall not be affected.

Article 29 When establishing a company, an application for establishment registration shall be filed with the company registration authority according to law.
Where laws or administrative regulations require that the establishment of a company must be approved, the approval procedures shall be completed according to law before the company registration.

Article 30 When applying for the establishment of a company, documents such as the application for establishment registration and the company's articles of association shall be submitted, and the submitted materials shall be authentic, lawful, and valid.
Where the application materials are incomplete or do not conform to the statutory form, the company registration authority shall inform the applicant of the materials to be supplemented in a single notice.

Article 31 Where an application for the establishment of a company meets the establishment conditions provided for in this Law, the company registration authority shall register it as a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company accordingly; where the establishment conditions provided for in this Law are not met, the company shall not be registered as a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company.

Article 33 A company established according to law shall be issued a company business license by the company registration authority. The date of issuance of the company business license shall be the date of incorporation of the company.
The company business license shall specify matters such as the company's name, domicile, registered capital, business scope, and name of the legal representative.
The company registration authority may issue an electronic business license. An electronic business license shall have the same legal effect as a paper business license.

Article 34 Where the registration items of a company change, the company shall undergo change registration according to law.
Where the registration items of a company have not been registered or have not been changed by registration, they shall not be invoked against a bona fide counterparty.

Article 35 When applying for change of registration, a company shall submit documents such as the application for change of registration signed by the company's legal representative and a lawfully adopted resolution or decision on the change to the company registration authority.
Where the change in registration items involves amendments to the company's articles of association, the amended articles of association shall be submitted.
Where a company changes its legal representative, the application for change of registration shall be signed by the new legal representative.
Article 36 Where the items recorded in the company business license change, after the company undergoes change registration, the company registration authority shall issue a new business license.

Article 37 Where a company needs to be terminated due to dissolution, bankruptcy declaration, or other statutory grounds, it shall apply to the company registration authority for cancellation of registration according to law, and the company registration authority shall announce the termination of the company.
Article 38 Where a company establishes a branch, it shall apply for registration with the company registration authority and obtain a business license.

Article 39 Where a company obtains establishment registration by reporting false registered capital, submitting false materials, or using other fraudulent means to conceal important facts, the company registration authority shall revoke the registration in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.

Article 41 Company registration authorities shall optimize the procedures for handling company registration, improve the efficiency of company registration, strengthen information technology development, promote convenient methods such as online processing, and enhance the facilitation of company registration.
The market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall, in accordance with this Law and relevant laws and administrative regulations, formulate specific measures for company registration.
Article 42 A limited liability company shall be established with contribution from not less than one and not more than fifty shareholders.

Article 43 The shareholders at the time of establishment of a limited liability company may enter into an establishment agreement to specify their respective rights and obligations during the process of company establishment.

Article 44 The legal consequences of the civil activities carried out by the shareholders at the time of establishment of a limited liability company for the purpose of establishing the company shall be borne by the company.
If the company is not established, the legal consequences shall be borne by the shareholders at the time of establishment; if there are two or more shareholders at the time of establishment, they shall enjoy joint and several claims and bear joint and several debts.
Where the shareholders at the time of establishment engage in civil activities in their own name for the purpose of establishing the company and thereby incur civil liability, a third party shall have the right to elect to request the company or the shareholders at the time of establishment to bear such liability.
If the shareholders at the time of establishment cause harm to others in the performance of their duties of establishing the company, after the company or the shareholders without fault have borne compensation liability, they may seek recourse against the shareholders at fault.
Article 45 To establish a limited liability company, the shareholders shall jointly formulate the company's articles of association.

Article 47 The registered capital of a limited liability company shall be the total amount of capital subscribed by all shareholders as registered with the company registration authority. The total amount of capital subscribed by all shareholders shall be fully paid by the shareholders within five years from the date of establishment of the company in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association.
Where laws, administrative regulations, or decisions of the State Council provide otherwise regarding the actual payment of registered capital, the minimum amount of registered capital, or the term of capital contribution by shareholders of a limited liability company, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 48 Shareholders may make capital contributions in currency, or in kind, intellectual property, land use rights, equity, debt claims, or other non-monetary property that can be valued in currency and transferred according to law, except for property that laws and administrative regulations provide shall not be used as capital contributions.
Non-monetary property used as capital contributions shall be appraised and valued, and the property shall be verified; the valuation shall not be overestimated or underestimated. Where laws and administrative regulations have provisions on appraisal and valuation, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 49 Shareholders shall pay in full and on time the amount of capital contribution each has subscribed under the company's articles of association.
If a shareholder makes a capital contribution in currency, the full amount of the currency contribution shall be deposited into the bank account opened by the limited liability company; if a shareholder makes a capital contribution in non-monetary property, the formalities for transfer of the property rights shall be handled according to law.
If a shareholder fails to pay the capital contribution in full and on time, in addition to paying the full amount to the company, it shall also bear compensation liability for the losses caused to the company.

Article 50 Where at the time of establishment of a limited liability company, a shareholder fails to actually pay the capital contribution in accordance with the company's articles of association, or the actual value of the non-monetary property actually contributed is significantly lower than the amount of capital contribution subscribed, the other shareholders at the time of establishment shall bear joint and several liability with such shareholder within the scope of the shortfall in capital contribution.

Article 51 After the establishment of a limited liability company, the board of directors shall verify the capital contribution status of the shareholders. If it discovers that a shareholder has failed to pay the capital contribution in full and on time as required by the company's articles of association, the company shall issue a written call for payment to such shareholder to demand the capital contribution.
If the obligation under the preceding paragraph is not fulfilled in a timely manner, causing losses to the company, the responsible directors shall bear compensation liability.

Article 52 Where a shareholder fails to pay the capital contribution by the date specified in the company's articles of association, and the company issues a written call for payment in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1 of the preceding article, the company may specify a grace period for the payment of the capital contribution; the grace period shall be not less than sixty days from the date the company issues the call for payment. If the shareholder still fails to perform the capital contribution obligation after the expiration of the grace period, the company may, by a resolution of the board of directors, issue a notice of loss of rights to such shareholder, and the notice shall be issued in writing. From the date of issuance of the notice, the shareholder shall lose its equity rights corresponding to the unpaid capital contribution.
The equity rights lost in accordance with the preceding paragraph shall be transferred according to law, or the registered capital shall be reduced accordingly and the equity rights shall be cancelled; if they are not transferred or cancelled within six months, the other shareholders of the company shall pay the corresponding capital contribution in full in proportion to their respective capital contribution ratios.
If a shareholder has any objection to the loss of rights, it shall file a lawsuit with the People's Court within thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice of loss of rights.

Article 53 After the establishment of the company, a shareholder shall not withdraw its capital contribution.
If the preceding paragraph is violated, the shareholder shall return the withdrawn capital contribution; if losses are caused to the company, the responsible directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall bear joint and several compensation liability with such shareholder.

Article 54 If a company is unable to repay its debts as they fall due, the company or the creditor of the matured claim shall have the right to demand that a shareholder who has subscribed for capital contribution but whose payment term has not yet arrived make an early payment of the capital contribution.

Article 57 A shareholder shall have the right to inspect and copy the company's articles of association, register of shareholders, minutes of shareholders' meetings, resolutions of the board of directors, resolutions of the board of supervisors, and financial and accounting reports.
A shareholder may request to inspect the company's accounting books and vouchers. Where a shareholder requests to inspect the company's accounting books and vouchers, it shall submit a written request to the company, stating the purpose. If the company has reasonable grounds to believe that the shareholder's inspection of the accounting books and vouchers has an improper purpose and may damage the company's legitimate interests, it may refuse to provide inspection, and shall provide a written reply to the shareholder within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the written request, stating the reasons. If the company refuses to provide inspection, the shareholder may file a lawsuit with the People's Court.
For inspection of the materials referred to in the preceding paragraph, the shareholder may entrust an accounting firm, law firm, or other intermediary institution to conduct the inspection.
When inspecting or copying relevant materials, the shareholder and the accounting firm, law firm, or other intermediary institution entrusted by it shall comply with laws and administrative regulations on the protection of state secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, personal information, etc.
Where a shareholder requests to inspect or copy relevant materials of a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, the provisions of the preceding four paragraphs shall apply.

Article 58 The shareholders' meeting of a limited liability company shall be composed of all shareholders. The shareholders' meeting is the power organ of the company and shall exercise its functions and powers in accordance with this Law.

Article 60 A limited liability company with only one shareholder shall not have a shareholders' meeting. When the shareholder makes a decision on the matters listed in paragraph 1 of the preceding Article, it shall adopt a written form, and after being signed or sealed by the shareholder, it shall be kept at the company.

Article 61 The first shareholders' meeting shall be convened and presided over by the shareholder who has made the largest capital contribution, and shall exercise its functions and powers in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 62 Shareholders' meetings shall be divided into regular meetings and interim meetings.
Regular meetings shall be convened on time in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association. Where shareholders representing one-tenth or more of the voting rights, one-third or more of the directors, or the board of supervisors propose to convene an interim meeting, an interim meeting shall be convened.

Article 63 A shareholders' meeting shall be convened by the board of directors and presided over by the chairman of the board; if the chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, the meeting shall be presided over by the vice chairman; if the vice chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, a director shall be jointly recommended by more than half of the directors to preside over the meeting.
If the board of directors is unable or fails to perform its duty to convene a shareholders' meeting, the board of supervisors shall convene and preside over the meeting; if the board of supervisors fails to convene and preside over the meeting, shareholders representing one-tenth or more of the voting rights may convene and preside over the meeting on their own.

Article 64 To convene a shareholders' meeting, all shareholders shall be notified fifteen days prior to the meeting; unless otherwise provided in the company's articles of association or otherwise agreed by all shareholders.
A shareholders' meeting shall prepare minutes of the decisions on matters discussed, and the shareholders present at the meeting shall sign or affix their seals to the minutes.

Article 65 At a shareholders' meeting, shareholders shall exercise their voting rights in proportion to their capital contributions; unless otherwise provided in the company's articles of association.

Article 66 The deliberation methods and voting procedures of a shareholders' meeting shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association, except as otherwise provided in this Law.
A resolution of a shareholders' meeting shall be adopted by shareholders representing more than half of the voting rights.
Resolutions of a shareholders' meeting on amending the company's articles of association, increasing or reducing the registered capital, and on merger, division, dissolution, or change of the company form, shall be adopted by shareholders representing two-thirds or more of the voting rights.

Article 68 The board of directors of a limited liability company shall consist of three or more members. Among the members, there may be representatives of the company's employees. For a limited liability company with 300 or more employees, unless it has a board of supervisors that includes employee representatives in accordance with the law, the board of directors shall include representatives of the company's employees. The employee representatives on the board of directors shall be democratically elected by the company's employees through the employee representative assembly, the employee assembly, or other forms.
The board of directors shall have one chairman, and may have a vice chairman. The method for the appointment of the chairman and vice chairman shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association.

Article 69 A limited liability company may, in accordance with the provisions of its articles of association, set up an audit committee composed of directors in the board of directors, which shall exercise the functions and powers of the board of supervisors as provided in this Law, and no board of supervisors or supervisor shall be set up. Employee representatives who are members of the board of directors may become members of the audit committee.

Article 70 The term of office of a director shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association, but each term shall not exceed three years. A director may be re-elected upon expiration of his term of office.
Where a director's term of office expires and no timely re-election is held, or where the resignation of a director within his term causes the number of directors to fall below the statutory number, before the newly elected director assumes office, the former director shall still perform the duties of a director in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association.
Where a director resigns, he shall notify the company in writing, and the resignation shall take effect on the date the company receives the notice; however, if the circumstance under the preceding paragraph exists, the director shall continue to perform his duties.

Article 71 The shareholders' meeting may resolve to remove a director, and the removal shall take effect on the date the resolution is made.
If a director is removed before the expiration of his term without just cause, the director may request the company to compensate him.

Article 72 Meetings of the board of directors shall be convened and presided over by the chairman of the board; if the chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, the meeting shall be convened and presided over by the vice chairman; if the vice chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, a director shall be jointly recommended by more than half of the directors to convene and preside over the meeting.

Article 73 The deliberation methods and voting procedures of the board of directors shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association, except as otherwise provided in this Law.
A meeting of the board of directors may be held only if more than half of the directors are present. A resolution of the board of directors shall be adopted by more than half of all directors.
Each director shall have one vote in the voting on a resolution of the board of directors.
The board of directors shall prepare minutes of the decisions on matters discussed, and the directors present at the meeting shall sign the minutes.

Article 74 A limited liability company may have a manager, who shall be appointed or dismissed by decision of the board of directors.
The manager shall be accountable to the board of directors and shall exercise his functions and powers in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association or the authorization of the board of directors. The manager shall attend meetings of the board of directors as a non-voting participant.

Article 75 A limited liability company that is relatively small in scale or has a relatively small number of shareholders may have one director instead of a board of directors, who shall exercise the functions and powers of the board of directors as provided in this Law. Such director may concurrently serve as the manager of the company.

Article 76 A limited liability company shall have a board of supervisors, except as otherwise provided in Articles 69 and 83 of this Law.
The board of supervisors shall consist of three or more members. The members of the board of supervisors shall include representatives of shareholders and an appropriate proportion of representatives of the company's employees, among which the proportion of employee representatives shall not be less than one-third, and the specific proportion shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association. The employee representatives on the board of supervisors shall be democratically elected by the company's employees through the employee representative assembly, the employee assembly, or other forms.
The board of supervisors shall have one chairperson, who shall be elected by more than half of all supervisors. The chairperson of the board of supervisors shall convene and preside over meetings of the board of supervisors; if the chairperson is unable or fails to perform his duties, a supervisor shall be jointly recommended by more than half of the supervisors to convene and preside over meetings of the board of supervisors.
Directors and senior officers shall not concurrently serve as supervisors.

Article 77 The term of office of a supervisor shall be three years. A supervisor may be re-elected upon expiration of his term of office.
Where a supervisor's term of office expires and no timely re-election is held, or where the resignation of a supervisor within his term causes the number of supervisors to fall below the statutory number, before the newly elected supervisor assumes office, the former supervisor shall still perform the duties of a supervisor in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association.

Article 79 A supervisor may attend meetings of the board of directors as a non-voting participant and may raise questions or make suggestions on matters resolved by the board of directors.
If the board of supervisors discovers any abnormality in the company's operations, it may conduct an investigation; if necessary, it may engage an accounting firm or other institution to assist in its work, with the expenses borne by the company.

Article 80 The board of supervisors may request directors and senior officers to submit reports on the performance of their duties.
Directors and senior officers shall truthfully provide relevant information and materials to the board of supervisors, and shall not obstruct the board of supervisors or any supervisor from exercising their functions and powers.

Article 81 The board of supervisors shall hold at least one meeting each year, and any supervisor may propose the convening of an interim meeting of the board of supervisors.
The deliberation methods and voting procedures of the board of supervisors shall be prescribed by the company's articles of association, except as otherwise provided in this Law.
A resolution of the board of supervisors shall be adopted by more than half of all supervisors.
Each supervisor shall have one vote in the voting on a resolution of the board of supervisors.
The board of supervisors shall prepare minutes of the decisions on matters discussed, and the supervisors present at the meeting shall sign the minutes.
Article 82 The necessary expenses incurred by the board of supervisors in exercising its functions and powers shall be borne by the company.

Article 83 A limited liability company with a relatively small scale or a relatively small number of shareholders may not set up a board of supervisors, but may have one supervisor to exercise the functions and powers of the board of supervisors as provided for in this Law; with the unanimous consent of all shareholders, it may also have no supervisor.

Article 84 Shareholders of a limited liability company may transfer all or part of their equity to each other.
Where a shareholder intends to transfer equity to a person other than a shareholder, the shareholder shall notify in writing the other shareholders of matters such as the quantity, price, payment method, and term of the equity transfer. Other shareholders shall have the right of first refusal under the same conditions. If a shareholder fails to reply within thirty days from the receipt of the written notice, the shareholder shall be deemed to have waived the right of first refusal. Where two or more shareholders exercise the right of first refusal, they shall negotiate to determine the respective proportion of the purchase; if negotiation fails, the right of first refusal shall be exercised in proportion to their respective capital contributions at the time of the transfer.
Where the company's articles of association have other provisions on equity transfer, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 85 Where the People's Court transfers a shareholder's equity in accordance with the compulsory execution procedures provided for by law, it shall notify the company and all shareholders. Other shareholders shall have the right of first refusal under the same conditions. If other shareholders do not exercise the right of first refusal within twenty days from the date of the notification by the People's Court, they shall be deemed to have waived the right of first refusal.

Article 86 Where a shareholder transfers equity, the shareholder shall notify the company in writing and request that the register of shareholders be updated; if change registration is required, the shareholder shall also request that the company handle the change registration with the company registration authority. If the company refuses or fails to respond within a reasonable period, the transferor and transferee may bring a lawsuit to the People's Court according to law.
Upon transfer of equity, the transferee may claim to exercise shareholders' rights against the company from the time the transferee is recorded in the register of shareholders.

Article 87 After the transfer of equity in accordance with this Law, the company shall promptly cancel the capital contribution certificate of the original shareholder, issue a capital contribution certificate to the new shareholder, and correspondingly amend the records in the company's articles of association and the register of shareholders concerning the shareholder and the amount of capital contribution contributed. Such amendment to the company's articles of association shall not require a vote by the shareholders' meeting.

Article 88 Where a shareholder transfers equity that has been subscribed but for which the capital contribution period has not yet matured, the transferee shall assume the obligation to pay such capital contribution; if the transferee fails to pay the capital contribution in full on time, the transferor shall bear supplementary liability for the portion of the capital contribution the transferee fails to pay on time.
Where a shareholder who has failed to pay capital contribution by the date specified in the company's articles of association or for whom the actual value of non-monetary property contributed as capital is significantly lower than the subscribed capital contribution transfers equity, the transferor and the transferee shall bear joint and several liability within the scope of the insufficient capital contribution; if the transferee neither knew nor should have known of the existence of the aforementioned circumstances, the transferor shall bear liability.

Article 89 In any of the following circumstances, a shareholder who voted against the resolution at the shareholders' meeting may request the company to purchase its equity at a reasonable price:
(1) The company has not distributed profits to shareholders for five consecutive years, during which the company has been profitable and meets the conditions for profit distribution as provided for in this Law;
(2) The company merges, divides, or transfers its main assets;
(3) The term of operation specified in the company's articles of association has expired or another event for dissolution specified in the articles of association has occurred, and the shareholders' meeting adopts a resolution to amend the articles of association to continue the company.
If the shareholder and the company fail to reach an equity purchase agreement within sixty days from the date the shareholders' meeting resolution is made, the shareholder may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within ninety days from the date the resolution is made.
Where a controlling shareholder of the company abuses its shareholder rights, causing serious damage to the interests of the company or other shareholders, other shareholders shall have the right to request the company to purchase their equity at a reasonable price.
The company's own equity purchased under the circumstances specified in paragraphs 1 and 3 of this Article shall be transferred or canceled according to law within six months.

Article 90 After the death of a natural person shareholder, the lawful successors thereof may inherit the shareholder status; however, this shall not apply if the company's articles of association provide otherwise.

Article 91 A joint stock limited company may be established by means of promotion or by means of public offering.
Promotion establishment means that the promoters subscribe for all the shares to be issued at the time of incorporation to establish the company.
Public offering establishment means that the promoters subscribe for a part of the shares to be issued at the time of incorporation and offer the remaining shares to specific targets or to the public.

Article 92 For the establishment of a joint stock limited company, there shall be no less than one and no more than 200 promoters, among whom more than half shall have domiciles within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 93 The promoters of a joint stock limited company shall undertake the preparatory matters of the company.
The promoters shall enter into a promoters' agreement to specify their respective rights and obligations in the process of the company's incorporation.
Article 94 For the establishment of a joint stock limited company, the promoters shall jointly draft the articles of association.

Article 96 The registered capital of a joint stock limited company shall be the total share capital of the issued shares registered with the company registration authority. Before the shares subscribed for by the promoters are fully paid in, shares shall not be offered to others.
Where the law, administrative regulations, and decisions of the State Council provide otherwise on the minimum registered capital of a joint stock limited company, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 97 Where a joint stock limited company is established by means of promotion, the promoters shall subscribe for the full amount of shares to be issued at the time of incorporation as specified in the articles of association.
Where a joint stock limited company is established by means of public offering, the shares subscribed for by the promoters shall not be less than 35% of the total number of shares to be issued at the time of incorporation as specified in the articles of association; however, where the law or administrative regulations provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 98 The promoters shall pay in full the subscription price for the shares subscribed for by them before the incorporation of the company.
The provisions of Articles 48 and 49(2) of this Law on capital contribution by shareholders of a limited liability company shall apply to the capital contribution of the promoters.

Article 99 Where a promoter fails to pay the subscription price for the shares subscribed for, or the actual value of the non-monetary property contributed as capital is obviously lower than the value of the shares subscribed for, the other promoters shall bear joint and several liability with such promoter to the extent of the deficiency in the capital contribution.

Article 100 Where promoters offer shares to the public, they shall publish a prospectus and prepare subscription forms. The subscription forms shall contain the matters specified in Article 154(2) and (3) of this Law, and shall be filled in by the subscribers with the number of shares subscribed for, the amount, and the domicile, and shall be signed or sealed by them. Subscribers shall pay the full subscription price for the shares subscribed for.

Article 101 After the full payment of the subscription price for the shares offered to the public, it shall be verified by a legally established capital verification institution which shall issue a certificate.

Article 103 The promoters of a joint stock limited company established by means of public offering shall convene the inaugural meeting within 30 days from the date when the full subscription price for the shares to be issued at the time of incorporation is paid in. The promoters shall notify each subscriber or make an announcement of the date of the meeting 15 days prior to its convening. The inaugural meeting may be held only if subscribers holding more than half of the voting rights are present.
For a joint stock limited company established by means of promotion, the convening of the inaugural meeting and the voting procedures shall be prescribed by the articles of association or the promoters' agreement.

Article 105 Where the shares to be issued at the time of incorporation are not fully subscribed, or after the full payment of the subscription price for the issued shares, the promoters fail to convene the inaugural meeting within 30 days, the subscribers may demand the promoters to refund the paid-in subscription price plus bank deposit interest for the same period.
After the promoters or subscribers have paid the subscription price or delivered the non-monetary property as capital contribution, they shall not withdraw their capital contribution, except in the circumstances where the shares are not subscribed for within the prescribed period, the promoters fail to convene the inaugural meeting within the prescribed period, or the inaugural meeting resolves not to establish the company.

Article 106 The board of directors shall authorize a representative to apply for incorporation registration with the company registration authority within 30 days after the conclusion of the inaugural meeting.
Article 107 The provisions of Articles 44, 49(3), 51, 52, and 53 of this Law shall apply to joint stock limited companies.

Article 108 When a limited liability company is converted into a joint stock limited company, the total amount of converted paid-in share capital shall not exceed the net assets of the company. Where a limited liability company is converted into a joint stock limited company and publicly issues shares to increase its registered capital, it shall be handled according to law.

Article 109 A joint stock limited company shall maintain at the company the company's articles of association, register of shareholders, minutes of shareholders' meetings, minutes of board of directors meetings, minutes of board of supervisors meetings, financial accounting reports, and register of bondholders.

Article 110 Shareholders have the right to consult and copy the company's articles of association, register of shareholders, minutes of shareholders' meetings, resolutions of the board of directors, resolutions of the board of supervisors, and financial accounting reports, and to make suggestions or inquiries regarding the company's operations.
Where a shareholder who, individually or jointly, holds three percent or more of the shares of the company for at least 180 consecutive days requests to consult the company's accounting books and accounting vouchers, the provisions of paragraphs 2, 3, and 4 of Article 57 of this Law shall apply. Where the company's articles of association provide for a lower shareholding percentage, such provision shall prevail.
Where a shareholder requests to consult or copy materials related to the company's wholly-owned subsidiaries, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply.
Where a shareholder of a listed company consults or copies relevant materials, it shall comply with the provisions of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 111 The shareholders' meeting of a joint stock limited company shall be composed of all shareholders. The shareholders' meeting is the authoritative body of the company and shall exercise its functions and powers in accordance with this Law.

Article 112 The provisions of paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 of Article 59 of this Law regarding the functions and powers of the shareholders' meeting of a limited liability company shall apply to the shareholders' meeting of a joint stock limited company.
The provisions of Article 60 of this Law regarding that a limited liability company with only one shareholder does not set up a shareholders' meeting shall apply to a joint stock limited company with only one shareholder.

Article 114 Shareholders' meetings shall be convened by the board of directors and presided over by the chairman of the board; if the chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, the meeting shall be presided over by the vice chairman; if the vice chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, a director jointly nominated by more than half of the directors shall preside over the meeting.
Where the board of directors is unable or fails to perform its duty of convening the shareholders' meeting, the board of supervisors shall promptly convene and preside over the meeting; if the board of supervisors fails to convene and preside over the meeting, shareholders individually or jointly holding ten percent or more of the company's shares for at least 90 consecutive days may convene and preside over the meeting on their own.
Where shareholders individually or jointly holding ten percent or more of the company's shares request the convening of an extraordinary shareholders' meeting, the board of directors and the board of supervisors shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of the request, decide whether to convene the extraordinary shareholders' meeting and reply to the shareholders in writing.

Article 115 For the convening of a shareholders' meeting, the time, place, and matters to be considered shall be notified to each shareholder at least twenty days prior to the meeting; for an extraordinary shareholders' meeting, notice shall be given at least fifteen days prior to the meeting.
Shareholders individually or jointly holding one percent or more of the company's shares may, ten days prior to the convening of the shareholders' meeting, propose an extraordinary proposal and submit it in writing to the board of directors. The extraordinary proposal shall have a clear topic and specific matters for resolution. The board of directors shall, within two days after receiving the proposal, notify the other shareholders and submit the extraordinary proposal to the shareholders' meeting for deliberation; except where the extraordinary proposal violates laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, or falls outside the scope of functions and powers of the shareholders' meeting. The company shall not increase the shareholding percentage requirement for shareholders to propose extraordinary proposals.
For companies that issue shares to the public, the notices specified in the preceding two paragraphs shall be made by way of public announcement.
The shareholders' meeting shall not adopt resolutions on matters not listed in the notice.

Article 116 When shareholders attend a shareholders' meeting, each share held shall have one voting right, except for holders of class shares. Shares held by the company in itself shall have no voting right.
For a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, such resolution shall be adopted by more than half of the voting rights held by the shareholders present at the meeting.
For a resolution to amend the articles of association, increase or decrease the registered capital, or for a resolution on the merger, division, dissolution, or change of the company's form, such resolution shall be adopted by two-thirds or more of the voting rights held by the shareholders present at the meeting.

Article 117 When the shareholders' meeting elects directors or supervisors, a cumulative voting system may be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting.
The term "cumulative voting system" as used in this Law means that in the election of directors or supervisors at a shareholders' meeting, each share carries as many voting rights as the number of directors or supervisors to be elected, and a shareholder may concentrate the voting rights held by him.

Article 118 Where a shareholder appoints an authorized agent to attend a shareholders' meeting, the matters, authority, and duration of the agency shall be clearly specified; the authorized agent shall submit a shareholder's power of attorney to the company and exercise the voting right within the scope of authorization.

Article 119 The shareholders' meeting shall keep minutes of the decisions on the matters discussed, and the presiding person and the directors present at the meeting shall sign the minutes. The minutes shall be kept together with the attendance register of the shareholders present and the powers of attorney for those attending by proxy.

Article 120 A joint stock limited company shall have a board of directors, except as otherwise provided in Article 128 of this Law.
The provisions of Articles 67, 68(1), 70, and 71 of this Law shall apply to joint stock limited companies.

Article 121 A joint stock limited company may, in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association, set up an audit committee composed of directors within the board of directors to exercise the functions and powers of the board of supervisors as provided in this Law, and may not set up a board of supervisors or supervisors.
An audit committee shall have three or more members, and a majority of the members shall not hold any position other than director in the company, nor have any relationship with the company that may affect their independent and objective judgment. Employee representatives among the members of the board of directors may become members of the audit committee.
Resolutions of the audit committee shall be adopted by a majority of the members of the audit committee.
Voting on resolutions of the audit committee shall be one vote per person.
The meeting procedures and voting procedures of the audit committee, except as provided in this Law, shall be specified in the articles of association.
A company may, in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association, set up other committees within the board of directors.

Article 122 The board of directors shall have one chairman, and may have a vice chairman. The chairman and vice chairman shall be elected by the board of directors with the affirmative votes of more than half of all directors.
The chairman shall convene and preside over the board meetings, and shall inspect the implementation of resolutions of the board of directors. The vice chairman shall assist the chairman in his work; if the chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, the vice chairman shall perform the duties; if the vice chairman is unable or fails to perform his duties, a director jointly nominated by more than half of the directors shall perform the duties.

Article 123 The board of directors shall hold at least two meetings each year, and each meeting shall be notified to all directors and supervisors at least ten days prior to the meeting.
Shareholders representing more than one-tenth of the voting rights, more than one-third of the directors, or the board of supervisors may propose the convening of an interim board meeting. The chairman shall, within ten days after receiving the proposal, convene and preside over the board meeting.
For the convening of an interim meeting, the board of directors may specify a different method and time limit for notification.

Article 124 A board meeting may be held only if more than half of the directors are present. Resolutions of the board of directors shall be adopted by more than half of all directors.
Voting on resolutions of the board of directors shall be one vote per director.
The board of directors shall keep minutes of the decisions on the matters discussed, and the directors present at the meeting shall sign the minutes.

Article 125 Directors shall attend board meetings in person; if a director is unable to attend due to a reason, he may appoint another director in writing to attend on his behalf, and the power of attorney shall specify the scope of authorization.
A director shall bear liability for the resolutions of the board of directors. Where a resolution of the board of directors violates laws, administrative regulations, the articles of association, or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, and causes serious losses to the company, the directors who participated in the resolution shall bear compensation liability to the company; if a director proves that he expressed dissent during the voting and the dissent is recorded in the minutes, such director may be exempted from liability.

Article 126 A joint stock limited company shall have a manager, who shall be appointed or dismissed by the board of directors.
The manager shall be responsible to the board of directors and exercise his functions and powers in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association or the authorization of the board of directors. The manager shall attend board meetings.
Article 127 The board of directors of a company may decide that a member of the board of directors may concurrently serve as the manager.

Article 128 A joint stock limited company of a relatively small scale or with a relatively small number of shareholders may not set up a board of directors, but shall have one director who shall exercise the functions and powers of the board of directors as provided in this Law. Such director may concurrently serve as the manager of the company.
Article 129 A company shall periodically disclose to its shareholders the remuneration received by directors, supervisors, and senior officers from the company.

Article 130 A company limited by shares shall establish a board of supervisors, unless otherwise provided in Article 121, paragraph 1 and Article 133 of this Law.
The board of supervisors shall consist of three or more members. The members of the board of supervisors shall include representatives of shareholders and an appropriate proportion of representatives of the company's employees, among which the proportion of employee representatives shall not be less than one-third. The specific proportion shall be stipulated in the company's articles of association. The employee representatives on the board of supervisors shall be democratically elected by the company's employees through the employee representative congress, employees' general meeting, or other forms.
The board of supervisors shall have one chairperson and may have a vice chairperson. The chairperson and vice chairperson of the board of supervisors shall be elected by a majority of all supervisors. The chairperson shall convene and preside over the meetings of the board of supervisors; if the chairperson is unable or fails to perform the duties, the vice chairperson shall convene and preside over the meetings of the board of supervisors; if the vice chairperson is unable or fails to perform the duties, more than half of the supervisors shall jointly nominate one supervisor to convene and preside over the meetings of the board of supervisors.
Directors and senior officers shall not concurrently serve as supervisors.
The provisions of Article 77 of this Law regarding the term of office of supervisors of a limited liability company shall apply to supervisors of a company limited by shares.

Article 131 The provisions of Articles 78 to 80 of this Law shall apply to the board of supervisors of a company limited by shares.
The expenses necessary for the board of supervisors to exercise its functions and powers shall be borne by the company.

Article 132 The board of supervisors shall hold a meeting at least once every six months. Supervisors may propose to convene an interim meeting of the board of supervisors.
The deliberation methods and voting procedures of the board of supervisors shall be stipulated in the company's articles of association, except as otherwise provided in this Law.
Resolutions of the board of supervisors shall be adopted by a majority of all supervisors.
Voting on resolutions of the board of supervisors shall be on a one-vote-per-supervisor basis.
The board of supervisors shall make minutes of the decisions on the matters discussed, and the supervisors present at the meeting shall sign the minutes.

Article 133 A company limited by shares with a relatively small scale or a small number of shareholders may, instead of establishing a board of supervisors, have one supervisor who shall exercise the functions and powers of the board of supervisors as provided in this Law.
Article 134 For the purposes of this Law, a 'listed company' refers to a company limited by shares whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange.

Article 135 Where a listed company purchases or sells major assets or provides guarantees to others within one year with an amount exceeding 30% of the company's total assets, a resolution shall be adopted by the shareholders' meeting and approved by more than two-thirds of the voting rights held by the shareholders present at the meeting.

Article 136 A listed company shall have independent directors. The specific administrative measures shall be formulated by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.
The articles of association of a listed company shall, in addition to the matters specified in Article 95 of this Law, also state the composition and functions of the special committees of the board of directors, as well as the remuneration assessment mechanisms for directors, supervisors, and senior officers, in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.

Article 138 A listed company shall have a secretary of the board of directors, who shall be responsible for the preparation of shareholders' meeting and board of directors meetings, the custody of documents, the management of the company's shareholder records, and handling matters such as information disclosure.

Article 139 Where a director of a listed company has a relationship with the enterprise or individual involved in the matter to be resolved at a board of directors meeting, the director shall promptly make a written report to the board of directors. The director with such a relationship shall not exercise the voting right on the resolution, nor shall he or she act as proxy for other directors to exercise voting rights. The board of directors meeting may be held only if more than half of the disinterested directors are present, and the resolution adopted at the board of directors meeting shall be approved by a majority of the disinterested directors. If the number of disinterested directors present at the board of directors meeting is less than three, the matter shall be submitted to the shareholders' meeting of the listed company for deliberation.

Article 140 A listed company shall, according to law, disclose information on its shareholders and actual controllers. The relevant information shall be true, accurate, and complete.
Holding shares of a listed company on behalf of another in violation of laws or administrative regulations is prohibited.

Article 141 A controlling subsidiary of a listed company shall not acquire shares of the listed company.
Where a controlling subsidiary of a listed company holds shares of the listed company due to reasons such as corporate merger or exercise of a pledge, it shall not exercise the voting rights attached to the shares held and shall promptly dispose of the relevant shares of the listed company.

Article 142 The capital of a company shall be divided into shares. All shares of the company shall, in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association, choose either par value shares or no-par value shares. Where par value shares are adopted, the amount of each share shall be equal.
A company may, in accordance with the provisions of its articles of association, convert all issued par value shares into no-par value shares or convert all no-par value shares into par value shares.
Where no-par value shares are adopted, not less than one-half of the proceeds from the issuance of shares shall be included in the registered capital.

Article 143 The issuance of shares shall follow the principles of fairness and impartiality. Each share of the same class shall have equal rights.
For shares of the same class issued in the same issuance, the issuance conditions and price per share shall be identical; the subscriber shall pay the same amount for each share subscribed.

Article 146 Where a company that issues class shares has matters specified in Article 116, paragraph 3 of this Law that may affect the rights of class shareholders, in addition to the resolution of the shareholders' meeting in accordance with Article 116, paragraph 3, such matters shall also be approved by more than two-thirds of the voting rights held by the shareholders present at the class shareholders' meeting.
The company's articles of association may stipulate other matters that require a resolution of the class shareholders' meeting.

Article 147 The shares of a company shall be in the form of share certificates. A share certificate is a document issued by the company to certify the shares held by a shareholder.
Share certificates issued by a company shall be registered share certificates.
Article 148 The issuance price of par value shares may be at par value or above par value, but shall not be below par value.

Article 149 Shares shall be in paper form or in such other form as prescribed by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.
Where shares are in paper form, the following main particulars shall be specified:
(1) the name of the company;
(2) the date of incorporation of the company or the time of issuance of the shares;
(3) the class of shares, the par value and the number of shares represented, and where shares without par value are issued, the number of shares represented by such shares.
Where shares are in paper form, the serial number of the share certificate shall also be specified, and it shall be signed by the legal representative and sealed by the company.
Where shares issued to promoters are in paper form, the words "promoters' shares" shall be indicated.

Article 150 After the incorporation of a joint stock limited company, it shall formally deliver share certificates to the shareholders. No share certificate shall be delivered to any shareholder before the incorporation of the company.

Article 152 The company's articles of association or the shareholders' meeting may authorize the board of directors to decide, within three years, to issue shares not exceeding fifty percent of the issued shares. However, if the capital contribution is made in non-monetary property, a resolution of the shareholders' meeting shall be required.
If the board of directors decides to issue shares in accordance with the preceding paragraph and such issuance results in changes to the registered capital or the number of issued shares, the amendment of the relevant provision in the articles of association shall not require a vote of the shareholders' meeting.

Article 153 Where the articles of association or the shareholders' meeting authorizes the board of directors to decide on the issue of new shares, the resolution of the board of directors shall be adopted by more than two-thirds of all directors.

Article 155 Where a company publicly offers shares to the public, it shall engage a securities company established according to law to underwrite the shares and shall enter into an underwriting agreement.

Article 156 Where a company publicly offers shares to the public, it shall enter into an agreement with a bank for the collection of subscription moneys.
The bank collecting the subscription moneys shall collect and hold the subscription moneys in accordance with the agreement, issue receipts to the subscribers who have paid the subscription moneys, and shall have the obligation to issue certificates of payment to the relevant authorities.
After the company has issued shares and fully collected the subscription moneys, it shall make a public announcement.

Article 157 Shares held by shareholders of a joint stock limited company may be transferred to other shareholders or to persons other than shareholders; if the articles of association impose restrictions on the transfer of shares, the transfer shall be carried out in accordance with the articles of association.
Article 158 A shareholder transferring his shares shall do so on a securities exchange established according to law or in such other manner as prescribed by the State Council.

Article 159 Transfer of shares shall be effected by the shareholder by endorsement or in such other manner as provided for by laws or administrative regulations; after the transfer, the company shall record the name or title and domicile of the transferee in the register of shareholders.
No change shall be made to the register of shareholders within twenty days prior to the convening of a shareholders' meeting or within five days prior to the record date for distribution of dividends decided by the company. Where laws, administrative regulations, or the securities regulatory authority under the State Council have other provisions on changes to the register of shareholders of a listed company, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 160 Shares issued prior to the public issuance of shares by a company shall not be transferred within one year from the date on which the company's shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange. Where laws, administrative regulations, or the securities regulatory authority under the State Council have other provisions on the transfer of shares of a listed company held by shareholders or actual controllers, those provisions shall prevail.
The directors, supervisors, and senior officers of a company shall report to the company their holdings of shares of the company and any changes thereto; the number of shares transferred each year during their term of office as determined at the time of appointment shall not exceed twenty-five percent of the total number of shares of the company held by them; the shares of the company held by them shall not be transferred within one year from the date on which the company's shares are listed and traded. Within six months after the resignation of the above-mentioned persons, they shall not transfer the shares of the company held by them. The articles of association may impose other restrictions on the transfer of shares of the company held by directors, supervisors, and senior officers.
Where shares are pledged within the period during which transfer is restricted by laws or administrative regulations, the pledgee shall not exercise the pledge within the restricted transfer period.

Article 163 A company shall not provide gifts, loans, guarantees, or other financial assistance to any other person for the purpose of acquiring shares of the company or its parent company, unless the company implements an employee share ownership plan.
For the benefit of the company, upon a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, or upon a resolution of the board of directors made in accordance with the authorization of the articles of association or the shareholders' meeting, the company may provide financial assistance to any other person for the purpose of acquiring shares of the company or its parent company, provided that the total cumulative amount of financial assistance shall not exceed ten percent of the total issued share capital. The resolution of the board of directors shall be adopted by more than two-thirds of all directors.
If any violation of the preceding two paragraphs causes losses to the company, the responsible directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall bear compensation liability.

Article 164 If a share certificate is stolen, lost, or destroyed, the shareholder may, in accordance with the public summons procedure prescribed by the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, request the People's Court to declare the share certificate void. After the People's Court has declared the share certificate void, the shareholder may apply to the company for a replacement share certificate.
Article 165 Shares of a listed company shall be listed and traded in accordance with relevant laws, administrative regulations, and the trading rules of the stock exchange.
Article 166 A listed company shall disclose relevant information in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 167 After the death of a natural person shareholder, his lawful successor may inherit the shareholder's status; except where otherwise provided in the articles of association of a joint stock limited company whose share transfer is restricted.

Article 168 The organizational structure of a state-funded company shall be governed by this Chapter; where this Chapter does not provide, other provisions of this Law shall apply.
For the purposes of this Law, a state-funded company refers to a wholly state-owned company or a company with state-owned capital controlled by the State, including a state-funded limited liability company and a joint stock limited company.

Article 169 For a state-funded company, the State Council or the local people's government shall, on behalf of the State, perform the duties of an investor according to law and enjoy the rights and interests of the investor. The State Council or the local people's government may authorize the state-owned assets supervision and administration institution or other departments or institutions to perform the duties of an investor on behalf of the people's government at the same level for state-funded companies.
Institutions and departments that perform the duties of an investor on behalf of the people's government at the same level are hereinafter collectively referred to as institutions performing the duties of an investor.

Article 170 The organization of the Communist Party of China in a state-invested company shall play a leading role in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Communist Party of China, study and discuss major operational and management matters of the company, and support the company's organizational structure in exercising its powers according to law.
Article 171 The articles of association of a wholly state-owned company shall be formulated by the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor.

Article 172 A wholly state-owned company shall not have a shareholders' meeting; the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor shall exercise the powers and functions of the shareholders' meeting. The institution performing the duties of the capital contributor may authorize the board of directors to exercise part of the powers and functions of the shareholders' meeting, but the formulation and amendment of the articles of association, merger, division, dissolution, application for bankruptcy, increase or decrease of registered capital, and distribution of profits shall be decided by the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor.

Article 173 The board of directors of a wholly state-owned company shall exercise its powers in accordance with this Law.
Among the members of the board of directors of a wholly state-owned company, more than half shall be external directors, and there shall be representatives of the company's employees.
The members of the board of directors shall be appointed by the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor; provided, however, that the representatives of the employees among the board members shall be elected by the company's employee representative congress.
The board of directors shall have one chairperson and may have one or more vice-chairpersons. The chairperson and vice-chairpersons shall be designated from among the board members by the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor.

Article 174 The manager of a wholly state-owned company shall be appointed or dismissed by the board of directors.
With the consent of the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor, a board member may concurrently serve as the manager.

Article 175 Directors and senior officers of a wholly state-owned company shall not hold concurrent positions in other limited liability companies, joint stock companies, or other economic organizations without the consent of the institution performing the duties of the capital contributor.

Article 176 Where a wholly state-owned company establishes an audit committee composed of directors within the board of directors to exercise the powers and functions of the board of supervisors as prescribed by this Law, it shall not establish a board of supervisors or supervisors.
Article 177 A state-invested company shall establish and improve internal supervision, management, and risk control systems according to law, and strengthen internal compliance management.
Article 179 Directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the company.

Article 180 Directors, supervisors, and senior officers owe a duty of loyalty to the company. They shall take measures to avoid conflicts of interest between themselves and the company, and shall not use their positions to seek improper benefits.
Directors, supervisors, and senior officers owe a duty of diligence to the company. In performing their duties, they shall exercise the reasonable care that a manager would ordinarily exercise in the best interests of the company.
Where a controlling shareholder or actual controller of the company does not serve as a director but actually executes the company's affairs, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply.

Article 182 Where a director, supervisor, or senior officer directly or indirectly enters into a contract or conducts a transaction with the company, they shall report matters relating to such contract or transaction to the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting and obtain a resolution approved by the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association.
