The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to the close relatives of a director, supervisor, or senior officer, any enterprise directly or indirectly controlled by a director, supervisor, senior officer, or their close relatives, and any related person who has other related relationships with a director, supervisor, or senior officer, when they enter into a contract or conduct a transaction with the company.

Article 184 Directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall not engage in or operate a business of the same type as that of the company in which they hold office, either for themselves or for others, unless they report to the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting and obtain a resolution approved by the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association.

Article 185 When the board of directors votes on matters set forth in Articles 182 through 184 of this Law, the interested directors shall not participate in the voting, and their voting rights shall not be counted in the total number of voting rights. If the number of disinterested directors attending the board meeting is less than three, the matter shall be submitted to the shareholders' meeting for deliberation.
Article 186 Any income derived by a director, supervisor, or senior officer from violating the provisions of Articles 181 through 184 of this Law shall belong to the company.

Article 187 If the shareholders' meeting requires directors, supervisors, and senior officers to attend the meeting, such directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall attend and accept inquiries from shareholders.

Article 188 Where a director, supervisor, or senior officer, in performing their duties, violates the provisions of any law, administrative regulation, or the articles of association, thereby causing losses to the company, they shall bear compensation liability.

Article 189 Where a director or senior officer falls under the circumstances set forth in the preceding Article, a shareholder of a limited liability company, or a shareholder who has continuously held one percent or more of the shares in a joint stock company individually or jointly for 180 days or more, may, in writing, request the board of supervisors to initiate a prosecution in a People's Court; where a supervisor falls under the circumstances set forth in the preceding Article, the aforementioned shareholder may, in writing, request the board of directors to initiate a prosecution in a People's Court.
If the board of supervisors or the board of directors, upon receiving the written request from the shareholder under the preceding paragraph, refuses to initiate a prosecution, or fails to initiate a prosecution within thirty days from the date of receiving the request, or if the situation is urgent and a failure to immediately initiate a prosecution would cause irreparable damage to the company's interests, the shareholder under the preceding paragraph shall have the right, in the company's interest, to directly initiate a prosecution in a People's Court in their own name.
Where any other person infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the company, causing losses to the company, the shareholder under paragraph 1 of this Article may initiate a prosecution in a People's Court in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs.
Where a director, supervisor, or senior officer of a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company falls under the circumstances set forth in the preceding Article, or where any other person infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, causing losses, a shareholder of the limited liability company, or a shareholder who has continuously held one percent or more of the shares in the joint stock company individually or jointly for 180 days or more, may, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding three paragraphs, request in writing the board of supervisors or board of directors of the wholly-owned subsidiary to initiate a prosecution in a People's Court, or directly initiate a prosecution in a People's Court in their own name.

Article 190 Where a director or senior officer violates the provisions of any law, administrative regulation, or the articles of association, thereby harming the interests of shareholders, the shareholders may initiate a prosecution in a People's Court.

Article 191 Where a director or senior officer, in performing their duties, causes damage to any other person, the company shall bear compensation liability; where the director or senior officer has acted with intent or gross negligence, they shall also bear compensation liability.

Article 192 Where a controlling shareholder or actual controller of a company instructs a director or senior officer to engage in any act that harms the interests of the company or the shareholders, they shall bear joint and several liability with such director or senior officer.

Article 193 A company may, during the tenure of a director, purchase liability insurance for compensation liability incurred by the director in performing the company's duties.
After the company purchases or renews liability insurance for a director, the board of directors shall report to the shareholders' meeting on matters such as the insured amount, scope of coverage, and premium rate of the liability insurance.

Article 194 Company bonds as referred to in this Law mean securities issued by a company that stipulate repayment of principal and payment of interest on a regular basis.
Company bonds may be issued publicly or privately.
The issuance and trading of company bonds shall comply with the provisions of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 196 Where a company issues company bonds in paper form, it shall state on the bonds the company name, face value, interest rate, repayment term, and other matters, and the bonds shall be signed by the legal representative and stamped with the company seal.
Article 197 Company bonds shall be registered bonds.
Article 199 The registration and settlement institution for company bonds shall establish relevant systems for bond registration, custody, interest payment, and redemption.

Article 200 Corporate bonds may be transferred, and the transfer price shall be agreed upon by the transferor and the transferee.
The transfer of corporate bonds shall comply with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 201 Corporate bonds shall be transferred by the bondholder by endorsement or by other methods prescribed by laws and administrative regulations; after the transfer, the company shall record the name or title and domicile of the transferee in the register of corporate bondholders.

Article 202 A joint stock limited company may, by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, or by a resolution of the board of directors authorized by the company's articles of association or the shareholders' meeting, issue corporate bonds convertible into shares and prescribe specific conversion methods. A listed company issuing corporate bonds convertible into shares shall register with the securities regulatory authority of the State Council.
Where corporate bonds convertible into shares are issued, the bonds shall be marked with the words "convertible corporate bonds" and the amount of convertible corporate bonds shall be stated in the register of corporate bondholders.

Article 203 Where corporate bonds convertible into shares are issued, the company shall, in accordance with the conversion methods, exchange shares for the bondholders, provided that the bondholders have the option to convert or not to convert the shares, unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 204 Where corporate bonds are publicly issued, a bondholders' meeting shall be established for the bondholders of the same series, and the procedures for convening the bondholders' meeting, meeting rules, and other important matters shall be specified in the bond offering method. The bondholders' meeting may pass resolutions on matters having an interest for the bondholders.
Unless otherwise agreed in the corporate bond offering method, the resolutions of the bondholders' meeting shall take effect for all bondholders of the same series.

Article 205 Where corporate bonds are publicly issued, the issuer shall engage a bond trustee for the bondholders to handle matters such as receiving repayment, preserving creditor's rights, litigation related to the bonds, and participating in the debtor's bankruptcy proceedings on behalf of the bondholders.

Article 206 The bond trustee shall perform its fiduciary duties diligently, responsibly, and fairly, and shall not harm the interests of the bondholders.
Where a conflict of interest between the trustee and the bondholders may harm the interests of the bondholders, the bondholders' meeting may pass a resolution to replace the bond trustee.
If a bond trustee violates laws, administrative regulations, or the resolutions of the bondholders' meeting, thereby harming the interests of the bondholders, it shall bear compensation liability.
Article 207 A company shall establish its own financial and accounting system in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the provisions of the financial department of the State Council.

Article 208 A company shall, at the end of each fiscal year, prepare financial and accounting reports and have them audited by an accounting firm according to law.
Financial and accounting reports shall be prepared in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the provisions of the financial department of the State Council.

Article 209 A limited liability company shall deliver financial and accounting reports to each shareholder within the time limit prescribed by the company's articles of association.
A joint stock limited company shall make its financial and accounting reports available at the company for inspection by shareholders twenty days before the convening of the annual shareholders' meeting; a joint stock limited company that has publicly issued shares shall announce its financial and accounting reports.

Article 210 When a company distributes its after-tax profits for the current year, it shall allocate ten percent of the profits to the statutory common reserve fund. Where the accumulated amount of the statutory common reserve fund reaches fifty percent or more of the company's registered capital, the company may no longer make such allocation.
If the statutory common reserve fund is insufficient to cover the losses of previous years, the company shall first use the current year's profits to cover the losses before allocating to the statutory common reserve fund in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
After allocating to the statutory common reserve fund from the after-tax profits, the company may, by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, also allocate to a discretionary common reserve fund from the after-tax profits.
The remaining after-tax profits after covering losses and making allocations to the common reserve fund shall be distributed as dividends: for a limited liability company, in proportion to the capital contributions actually paid by the shareholders, unless all shareholders agree not to distribute in proportion to capital contributions; for a joint stock limited company, in proportion to the shares held by the shareholders, unless otherwise provided by the company's articles of association.
No profits shall be distributed on shares held by the company itself.

Article 211 If a company distributes profits to shareholders in violation of the provisions of this Law, the shareholders shall return the profits distributed in violation of the provisions to the company; if losses are caused to the company, the shareholders and the responsible directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall bear compensation liability.
Article 212 If the shareholders' meeting passes a resolution to distribute profits, the board of directors shall make the distribution within six months from the date of the resolution.

Article 213 The premium income derived from issuing shares at an issue price exceeding the par value of the shares, the amount of proceeds from issuing shares without par value that is not included in the registered capital, and other items that the financial department of the State Council prescribes shall be included in the capital common reserve fund, shall be listed as the company's capital common reserve fund.

Article 214 The common reserve fund of a company shall be used to cover the company's losses, expand the company's production and operations, or be converted to increase the company's registered capital.
When using the common reserve fund to cover the company's losses, the discretionary common reserve fund and the statutory common reserve fund shall be used first; if the losses still cannot be covered, the capital common reserve fund may be used in accordance with the regulations.
When the statutory common reserve fund is converted to increase the registered capital, the remaining amount of such reserve fund shall not be less than twenty-five percent of the company's registered capital before the conversion.

Article 215 The engagement and dismissal of an accounting firm to undertake the company's audit business shall be decided by the shareholders' meeting, the board of directors, or the board of supervisors in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association.
When the company's shareholders' meeting, board of directors, or board of supervisors votes on the dismissal of an accounting firm, the accounting firm shall be allowed to state its opinions.

Article 216 A company shall provide the engaged accounting firm with truthful and complete accounting vouchers, accounting books, financial and accounting reports, and other accounting materials, and shall not refuse to provide, conceal, or make false reports.

Article 217 A company shall not maintain any accounting books other than the statutory accounting books.
No accounts for company funds shall be opened and deposited in any individual's name.

Article 218 A merger of companies may take the form of an absorption merger or a consolidation merger.
Where one company absorbs other companies, it is an absorption merger, and the absorbed company shall be dissolved. Where two or more companies merge to establish a new company, it is a consolidation merger, and all parties to the merger shall be dissolved.

Article 219 Where a company merges with a company in which it holds ninety percent or more of the shares, the merged company need not pass a resolution by its shareholders' meeting, but it shall notify the other shareholders, who shall have the right to request the company to purchase their equity interests or shares at a reasonable price.
Where the price paid in a merger does not exceed ten percent of the company's net assets, the merger may be effected without a resolution of the shareholders' meeting; however, this does not apply if the company's articles of association provide otherwise.
Where a company effects a merger without a resolution of the shareholders' meeting in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs, the merger shall be approved by a resolution of the board of directors.

Article 220 In the merger of companies, the merging parties shall conclude a merger agreement and prepare a balance sheet and a detailed list of assets. The company shall, within ten days from the date of the resolution on the merger, notify its creditors, and shall, within thirty days, make a public announcement in a newspaper or on the national enterprise credit information publicity system. Creditors may, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice or, if they have not received the notice, within forty-five days from the date of the public announcement, require the company to repay its debts or provide corresponding guarantees.
Article 221 In the merger of companies, the claims and debts of the merging parties shall be succeeded to by the company that continues to exist after the merger or by the newly established company.

Article 222 In the division of a company, its property shall be divided accordingly.
In the division of a company, a balance sheet and a detailed list of assets shall be prepared. The company shall, within ten days from the date of the resolution on the division, notify its creditors, and shall, within thirty days, make a public announcement in a newspaper or on the national enterprise credit information publicity system.

Article 223 The debts of a company prior to its division shall be borne jointly and severally by the companies after the division, unless otherwise agreed in a written agreement reached between the company and its creditors on the repayment of the debts before the division.

Article 224 A company reducing its registered capital shall prepare a balance sheet and a detailed list of assets.
The company shall, within ten days from the date of the resolution by the shareholders' meeting on the reduction of registered capital, notify its creditors, and shall, within thirty days, make a public announcement in a newspaper or on the national enterprise credit information publicity system. Creditors shall have the right, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice or, if they have not received the notice, within forty-five days from the date of the public announcement, to require the company to repay its debts or provide corresponding guarantees.
Where a company reduces its registered capital, the amount of capital contributions or shares shall be correspondingly reduced in proportion to the shareholders' capital contributions or shareholdings, unless otherwise provided by law, otherwise agreed by all shareholders of a limited liability company, or otherwise provided by the articles of association of a joint stock limited company.

Article 225 Where a company still has losses after making up losses in accordance with Article 214, paragraph 2 of this Law, it may reduce its registered capital to make up the losses. Where the registered capital is reduced to make up losses, the company shall not distribute any distributions to shareholders, nor shall it exempt shareholders from their obligation to make capital contributions or pay for shares.
Where the registered capital is reduced in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the provisions of paragraph 2 of the preceding article shall not apply, but the company shall, within thirty days from the date of the resolution by the shareholders' meeting on the reduction of registered capital, make a public announcement in a newspaper or on the national enterprise credit information publicity system.
After a company reduces its registered capital in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs, it shall not distribute profits until the accumulated amount of the statutory common reserve fund and the discretionary common reserve fund reaches fifty percent of the company's registered capital.

Article 226 Where the registered capital is reduced in violation of the provisions of this Law, the shareholders shall refund the funds they have received, and any reduction of shareholders' capital contributions shall be restored to the original state; if losses are caused to the company, the shareholders and the responsible directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall bear compensation liability.

Article 227 When a limited liability company increases its registered capital, shareholders shall have the right to subscribe for the new capital contributions in proportion to their actual paid-in capital contributions under the same terms and conditions, unless all shareholders agree not to exercise the preemptive right to subscribe in proportion to their capital contributions.
When a joint stock limited company issues new shares to increase its registered capital, shareholders shall not have preemptive subscription rights, unless otherwise provided by the company's articles of association or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting grants shareholders preemptive subscription rights.

Article 228 When a limited liability company increases its registered capital, the subscription of new capital contributions by shareholders shall be governed by the relevant provisions on making capital contributions for the establishment of a limited liability company in accordance with this Law.
When a joint stock limited company issues new shares to increase its registered capital, the subscription of new shares by shareholders shall be governed by the relevant provisions on payment for shares for the establishment of a joint stock limited company in accordance with this Law.

Article 230 Where a company has a circumstance specified in items (1) or (2) of paragraph 1 of the preceding article and has not yet distributed property to shareholders, the company may continue to exist by amending its articles of association or adopting a resolution by the shareholders' meeting.
For the amendment of the articles of association or the adoption of a resolution by the shareholders' meeting in accordance with the preceding paragraph, a limited liability company shall require approval by shareholders holding more than two-thirds of the voting rights, and a joint stock limited company shall require approval by shareholders holding more than two-thirds of the voting rights of the shareholders present at the shareholders' meeting.

Article 231 Where serious difficulties arise in the operation and management of a company, the continued existence of which would cause significant losses to the interests of shareholders and cannot be resolved through other means, shareholders holding more than ten percent of the voting rights of the company may request the People's Court to dissolve the company.

Article 232 Where a company is dissolved under items (1), (2), (4), or (5) of paragraph 1 of Article 229 of this Law, it shall undergo liquidation. The directors shall be the persons obligated to carry out liquidation and shall, within fifteen days from the date the ground for dissolution arises, form a liquidation group to conduct the liquidation.
The liquidation group shall be composed of directors, unless otherwise provided by the company's articles of association or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting appoints other persons.
Where the persons obligated to carry out liquidation fail to perform their liquidation duties in a timely manner, causing losses to the company or creditors, they shall bear compensation liability.

Article 233 Where a company is required to undergo liquidation in accordance with paragraph 1 of the preceding article but fails to form a liquidation group within the prescribed time limit to conduct liquidation, or does not conduct liquidation after forming a liquidation group, interested parties may apply to the People's Court to designate relevant persons to form a liquidation group to conduct the liquidation. The People's Court shall accept the application and shall promptly organize the liquidation group to conduct the liquidation.
Where a company is dissolved under item (4) of paragraph 1 of Article 229 of this Law, the department that made the decision to revoke the business license, order the closure, or revoke the company, or the company registration authority, may apply to the People's Court to designate relevant persons to form a liquidation group to conduct the liquidation.

Article 235 The liquidation group shall, within ten days from its establishment, notify creditors, and shall, within sixty days, make a public announcement in a newspaper or on the national enterprise credit information publicity system. Creditors shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice or, if they have not received the notice, within forty-five days from the date of the public announcement, declare their claims to the liquidation group.
When creditors declare their claims, they shall state the relevant matters of the claims and provide supporting materials. The liquidation group shall register the claims.
During the period for declaring claims, the liquidation group shall not repay any creditor.

Article 236 After the liquidation group has sorted out the company's property and prepared a balance sheet and a detailed list of assets, it shall formulate a liquidation plan and submit it to the shareholders' meeting or the People's Court for confirmation.
The remaining property of the company, after the separate payment of liquidation expenses, employees' wages, social insurance premiums, and statutory compensation, the payment of taxes owed, and the settlement of the company's debts, shall be distributed to shareholders of a limited liability company in proportion to their capital contributions, and to shareholders of a joint stock limited company in proportion to their shareholdings.
During the liquidation period, the company shall continue to exist, but shall not engage in any business activities unrelated to the liquidation. The company's property shall not be distributed to shareholders until it has been used to settle debts in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 237 Where the liquidation group, after sorting out the company's property and preparing a balance sheet and a detailed list of assets, finds that the company's property is insufficient to pay off its debts, it shall apply to the People's Court for bankruptcy liquidation according to law.
After the People's Court accepts the bankruptcy application, the liquidation group shall transfer the liquidation matters to the bankruptcy administrator designated by the People's Court.

Article 238 The members of the liquidation group shall, in performing their liquidation duties, bear the duty of loyalty and the duty of diligence.
Where a member of the liquidation group fails to perform liquidation duties, causing losses to the company, he or she shall bear compensation liability; if losses are caused to creditors due to intentional acts or gross negligence, he or she shall bear compensation liability.

Article 239 After the conclusion of the company liquidation, the liquidation group shall prepare a liquidation report, submit it to the shareholders' meeting or the People's Court for confirmation, and submit it to the company registration authority, applying for the cancellation of the company registration.

Article 240 Where a company has not incurred any debts during its existence, or has fully settled all debts, it may, upon the undertaking of all shareholders, cancel the company registration through simplified procedures in accordance with the regulations.
To cancel company registration through simplified procedures, a public announcement shall be made on the national enterprise credit information publicity system, with a publicity period of not less than twenty days. After the expiry of the publicity period, if there is no objection, the company may apply to the company registration authority for the cancellation of company registration within twenty days.
Where a company cancels its company registration through simplified procedures, and the shareholders' undertaking regarding the content specified in paragraph 1 of this article is untrue, they shall bear joint and several liability for the debts incurred before the cancellation of the registration.

Article 241 Where a company's business license has been revoked, or the company has been ordered to close down or has been revoked, and it has not applied to the company registration authority for cancellation of company registration for three full years, the company registration authority may make a public announcement on the national enterprise credit information publicity system, with a publicity period of not less than sixty days. After the expiry of the publicity period, if there is no objection, the company registration authority may cancel the company registration.
Where the company registration is cancelled in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the liability of the former shareholders and the persons obligated to carry out liquidation of the company shall not be affected.
Article 242 Where a company is declared bankrupt according to law, bankruptcy liquidation shall be carried out in accordance with the laws on enterprise bankruptcy.
Article 243 For the purposes of this Law, a foreign company refers to a company established outside the People's Republic of China in accordance with the laws of a foreign country.

Article 244 Where a foreign company establishes a branch within the territory of the People's Republic of China, it shall submit an application to the competent authority of China and submit its articles of association, the certificate of company registration of the country to which it belongs, and other relevant documents. After obtaining approval, it shall register with the company registration authority according to law and obtain a business license.
The measures for the examination and approval of branches of foreign companies shall be formulated separately by the State Council.

Article 245 Where a foreign company establishes a branch within the territory of the People's Republic of China, it shall designate a representative or agent within the territory of the People's Republic of China to be responsible for the branch, and shall allocate to the branch funds commensurate with the business activities in which it engages.
If a minimum amount of operating funds is required for the branch of a foreign company, the State Council shall separately provide for it.

Article 246 A branch of a foreign company shall indicate in its name the nationality of the foreign company and its form of liability.
A branch of a foreign company shall keep the articles of association of the foreign company in its office.

Article 247 A branch established within the territory of the People's Republic of China by a foreign company shall not have the status of a Chinese legal person.
The foreign company shall bear civil liability for the business activities carried out by its branch within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 248 An approved branch of a foreign company shall, when engaging in business activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China, comply with the laws of China and shall not harm the public interests of Chinese society, and its lawful rights and interests shall be protected by Chinese law.

Article 249 Where a foreign company cancels its branch within the territory of the People's Republic of China, it shall settle its debts according to law and conduct liquidation in accordance with the provisions of this Law on company liquidation procedures. Before the debts are fully settled, the property of the branch shall not be transferred outside the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 250 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a company obtains company registration by making false declarations of registered capital, submitting false materials, or adopting other fraudulent means to conceal material facts, the company registration authority shall order the company to make corrections; for a company with false declarations of registered capital, a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 15% of the falsely declared registered capital shall be imposed; for a company that submitted false materials or adopted other fraudulent means to conceal material facts, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the business license shall be revoked; the directly responsible senior officer and other directly responsible persons shall be fined not less than 30,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan.

Article 251 Where a company fails to publish relevant information in accordance with Article 40 of this Law or fails to truthfully publish such information, the company registration authority shall order the company to make corrections and may impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan. If the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed; the directly responsible senior officer and other directly responsible persons shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 252 Where the promoters or shareholders of a company make false capital contributions, or fail to deliver or fail to deliver on time the currency or non-monetary property as capital contributions, the company registration authority shall order them to make corrections and may impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 15% of the falsely contributed amount or the unpaid contribution amount shall be imposed; the directly responsible senior officer and other directly responsible persons shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 253 Where the promoters or shareholders of a company, after the establishment of the company, withdraw their capital contributions, the company registration authority shall order them to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 15% of the withdrawn capital contribution amount; the directly responsible senior officer and other directly responsible persons shall be fined not less than 30,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan.

Article 255 Where a company, during a merger, division, reduction of registered capital, or liquidation, fails to notify or make a public announcement to creditors in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the company registration authority shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan on the company.

Article 256 Where a company, during liquidation, conceals property, makes false entries in the balance sheet or the detailed list of assets, or distributes company property before settling debts, the company registration authority shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 10% of the amount of concealed property or the amount of property distributed before settling debts; the directly responsible senior officer and other directly responsible persons shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 257 Where an institution undertaking asset appraisal, capital verification, or certification provides false materials or reports with material omissions, it shall be punished by the relevant department in accordance with the "Asset Appraisal Law of the People's Republic of China", the "Certified Public Accountants Law of the People's Republic of China", and other laws and administrative regulations.
Where an institution undertaking asset appraisal, capital verification, or certification causes losses to the company's creditors due to the inaccuracy of the appraisal results, capital verification, or certification certificates it has issued, it shall bear compensation liability within the scope of the inaccurate amount of its appraisal or certification, unless it can prove that it is not at fault.

Article 258 Where a company registration authority fails to perform its duties or improperly performs its duties in violation of laws and administrative regulations, administrative sanctions shall be imposed on the responsible leaders and directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 259 Where, without being registered as a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company according to law, a person falsely uses the name of a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, or without being registered as a branch of a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company according to law, a person falsely uses the name of a branch of a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, the company registration authority shall order it to make corrections or close it down, and may concurrently impose a fine of not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 260 Where a company, after its establishment, fails to commence business for more than six months without a justifiable reason, or, after commencing business, ceases business for six consecutive months or more, the company registration authority may revoke its business license, unless the company has undergone the procedures for suspension of operations according to law.
Where a company fails to undergo the relevant change of registration procedures in accordance with the provisions of this Law when changes occur in the registered items, the company registration authority shall order it to register within a specified time limit; if it fails to register within the time limit, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 261 Where a foreign company, in violation of the provisions of this Law, arbitrarily establishes a branch within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the company registration authority shall order it to make corrections or close it down, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.
Article 262 Where the name of a company is used to engage in serious illegal activities that endanger national security or public interests, the business license shall be revoked.

Article 263 Where a company, in violation of the provisions of this Law, shall bear civil compensation liability and pay fines and penalties, and its property is insufficient to pay, it shall first bear the civil compensation liability.
Article 264 Where the provisions of this Law are violated and a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 265 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms have the meanings set forth below:
(1) Senior officer refers to the manager, deputy manager, and financial officer of a company, the secretary of the board of directors of a listed company, and other persons specified in the company's articles of association.
(2) Controlling shareholder refers to a shareholder whose capital contribution accounts for more than 50% of the total capital of a limited liability company or whose shares held account for more than 50% of the total share capital of a joint stock limited company; or a shareholder whose capital contribution or shareholding ratio is less than 50% but whose voting rights derived from its capital contribution or shares held are sufficient to have a significant impact on the resolutions of the shareholders' meeting.
(3) Actual controller refers to a person who can actually control the conduct of a company through investment relationships, agreements, or other arrangements.
(4) Affiliated relationship refers to the relationship between the controlling shareholder, actual controller, directors, supervisors, and senior officers of a company and the enterprises directly or indirectly controlled by them, as well as any other relationship that may lead to the transfer of the company's interests. However, enterprises controlled by the state shall not be deemed to have an affiliated relationship solely because they are both under the control of the state.

Article 266 This Law shall come into force on July 1, 2024.
For companies that have been registered and established before the coming into force of this Law, if the term for capital contribution exceeds the time limit stipulated in this Law, it shall be gradually adjusted to within the time limit stipulated in this Law, unless otherwise provided by laws, administrative regulations, or the State Council; for those with manifestly abnormal capital contribution terms or amounts, the company registration authority may require them to make timely adjustments according to law. Specific implementation measures shall be formulated by the State Council.
